request.spec:
A claim can be commented (a text entry and a button on the claim; an empty comment is refused
with an error on the claim). Each comment is kept with the user who wrote it and the sheet's today
when it was written, shown on the claim in order as <user> on <date>: <text>, and written as
COMMENT_ADDED, naming the claim like every claim line and ending text=<text>. A viewer, an archived
sheet and the as-of view refuse it like any change.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
A claim can be commented (a text entry and a button on the claim; an empty comment is refused
with an error on the claim). Each comment is kept with the user who wrote it and the sheet's today
when it was written, shown on the claim in order as <user> on <date>: <text>, and written as
COMMENT_ADDED, naming the claim like every claim line and ending text=<text>. A viewer, an archived
sheet and the as-of view refuse it like any change.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
Claims can now be commented, and all 4 Playwright tests pass under `bin/e2e`.

**How it works**
- **Storage:** a new migration, `V55__claim_comment.sql`, adds a `claim_comment` table. Each row holds the claim, who wrote it, the sheet's today at the time, and the text. The table is wired into the as-of history like the claim's status log, so viewing the sheet as of an earlier date shows the comments as they stood then.
- **Server:** a new endpoint, `POST /api/sheets/{sheetId}/claims/{claimId}/comments`. A blank or whitespace-only comment gets a 400 and writes nothing to the store or the audit file. A comment that goes through is written to the audit file as `COMMENT_ADDED sheet=… by=… person=… amount=… date=… [number=…] text=…`, in the same form as other claim lines. Each claim the server returns now includes its comments, oldest first, as `<user> on <date>: <text>`.
- **Refusals:** viewers and archived sheets are already blocked by the existing request guard, and the as-of view is blocked in the front end, so comments needed no extra code for those cases.
- **Front end:** each claim row has a comment box (`claim-comment-text`), a Comment button (`claim-comment-add`) and its list of comments (`claim-comments-line`). A refusal shows in the row's existing `claim-error`, which clears when you type in the box or take the next action on that claim.

**Decisions to check**
- Comment text is trimmed before it is saved and audited.
- Comments are allowed on claims in any status, including SETTLED (the test relies on this). They are also allowed on claims in a closed period, because the request didn't say to block them.

One unrelated change: I added a `comments` field to the claim response, so every place that builds that response was updated. The responses for newly created and split claims always send an empty comment list, since a new claim has no comments yet.
